poster.note: The lighthouse on legs straddles the low sun: a silhouette you can name in five words, lit by a sun you can see, with a calm bottom strip and bottom-left. The sun disc is a free colour and only its glow gradient measures as guarded, far above the caption. The 2:3 and 1:1 were recomposed in the renderer, not cropped. Light band is light (L .526), so it should not sit beside another light plate.

focus.note: 0.655,0.30 sits on the hips with the sun between the legs. The lighthouse and sun hold in every wall.py shape, from the 577x163 strip to the 140x305 column, and in a 4:3 crop.

icon.note: Only the head, red band, four legs and one pale sun, drawn for 46. Reads on night and linen and does not look like a generic symbol.

emblem.note: Newly drawn with fewer parts (two legs, a bigger sun), not the icon scaled down. Holds at 30 px on both grounds.

keyStill.note: The great shell with the sun a finger above its lip: real tension ("you left just before the sun sat"), centred, with the poster's finish. The fan still reads at 132x66.

result.note: The payoff is right (Aurora before the full wall) and the middle 720 carries her and four panels. At 800x176, though, the six photographs read as white-speckled smudges; if a lit angle lets the prints read, take it.

gallery.note: Slide 04 is a plank-thin Lluna in a flat noon-blue sky (C .615, loud). It is a dot at 100 px and close to a plain engine frame that loses the look, so recompose it tighter. Slide 03 misses "the bottom 26 px calm" because of the checkerboard floor: raise the camera or crop a hedge or wall base into the bottom. 01, 02, 05 and 06 are strong.

seals.note: Twelve moments plus the event, each in three states drawn in the world (dusk / blue hour / graphite sketch), with no gold, padlock or text. Feat, collection and event outlines read apart at 32 px. Weakest at 32 px: doves-round-the-tower (reads as a totem) and lluna (a bent bar). Progress on night is almost black at 32 px. The collection outline echoes Gob's taped tag (see copying).

store.note: Five looks-only items: one centred item each, in cut paper on the sketchbook page, top corners calm, all readable at 40 px and in greyscale. No gold or guarded fills.

passTile.note: The sketchbook as the tile, with the world's ground, no price and a blank label. The pass name is optional and can be lettered once the lockup exists.

passGrounds.note: Bare page, cobalt gouache and night trencadís: three clearly different tiers, wordless and with no guarded fills.

marker.note: A taped print, dangling (next) and taped flat (held). Drawn for 48, counts nothing, and reads on a rail.

passRewards.note: Nine full-art rewards in the world's own objects (tape, stickers, a stamp, a lantern, a cap) that read at 120 px on their tier grounds. Nothing is dimmed and there are no counts.

owned.note: "Taped in": a 620 ms ES module that starts at once, plays once and ends on the held frame. The verb belongs to this world, there is no gold, and the held frame reads at 40 px.

update.note: One change, the residents turning to face you, shown with Quim square to the camera in the eye door, in the poster's light. It reads at 104x52 and has no version or NEW. The 308x154 thumb was recomposed, not cropped.

event.note: Festival night is clearly different from the poster. The left 45% is calm dark sky with no hot colour where Join sits, and the right 55% (crowd and fireworks) tells the event alone. The scallop event seal is distinct from the moment seals at 32 px.

living.note: In my own Playwright run it recomposed at every size from 120x90 to 900x200 with no stretching, no errors and 0.1 to 1.3 ms a frame. Anchor (0.656,0.33), and the held frame matches the poster. One small note: the shutter iris drops the whole plate dark for about 0.17 s once per 6.4 s loop (hover only), a light-band dip to keep this short.

backdrop.note: The bay at rest in one light, its horizon running on from the poster's, with no competing focal point and nothing hot by the rail. The phone version is composed separately (the Mirador floor), and the poster leads on both.

share.note: The art is right (poster register, subject at x 0.71, quiet bottom band, no ember), but the must "the one place the game's title lettering sits on the art" is unmet: no title is lettered. Add it in the plain upper-left sky once the lockup exists.

chip.note: Drawn for 64 with more parts than the icon (knees, feet in the cobalt bay, sun glints) and far fewer than the poster.

phone.note: Recomposed in the renderer at lens 34, not a crop: the same one image and register. It runs lighter (L .674).

lockup.note: There is no title-lockup.png. The game's drawTitle needs Caprasimo, which the sandbox could not load. Render it in a real browser, state its minimum width, then use it on the share card.

overall: A strong, coherent pass: every scene is a fresh frame from the game's own gouache renderer in one low western sun, and every drawn piece shares one cut-paper-on-sketchbook language, made with the game's own 2D code. The poster is a clean silhouette that survives every wall shape. What remains is lettering (no lockup, so the share card has no title) and two gallery slides.
copying: No outright copying and no reused pixels. Two borderline echoes of Arm B examples: (1) the seal-kind scheme (round coin / taped square / scallop) mirrors Gob's coin / taped tag / scalloped cookie, and Gob's notYours names "the taped tag"; the chat grounds it in the game's own washi tape, trencadís and great shell. (2) The store and pass ground is ruled cream paper like Carbon's tile (notYours: ruled paper with the orange margin line); there is no margin line, and the chat cites the game's own sketchbook style.css, which I could not check here.
made: Renderer: posters (2:1, 2:3, 1:1, 9:16), key still, result, gallery, update, event banner, backdrops and share card are new frames from the game's own WebGL renderer (studio build driven by render.js). Code: icon, emblem, chip, seals, store, pass and marker were drawn with the game's own Canvas 2D code (paint.js textures, people_paint.js figures) in Chromium via Playwright; the owned mark is a Canvas 2D ES module; the moving poster is a hand-written Canvas 2D board module. Title lettering was not made.
